clue.text: Almost broke, English woman welcoming offspring's building skill

indicators.note: almost means the word for broke is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: stony broke, often just stony, is British slang for having no money

indicators.note: a woman welcoming someone takes them in, so one name wraps round the other

parts.note: Mary is a woman's name
offspring's here reads as offspring is; a son is offspring

explanation.surface: A nearly penniless Englishwoman takes in her child's construction expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: STONY is British slang for broke (from 'stony broke'); 'Almost' trims it to STON. MARY 'welcoming' SON gives MASONRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Masonry work with cut stone is a trade craft used in constructing buildings.

clue.text: Unaccompanied male operating, a wise man

parts.note: a solo performance is done unaccompanied
a machine that is on is operating

explanation.surface: A man working alone is described as a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical King Solomon is proverbial for wisdom, so his name stands for any sage.

clue.text: Hold forth about gang leader, getting shot

indicators.note: the words for holding forth go about, that is around, the gang leader

parts.note: to opine is to state one's views, to hold forth
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, is the crossword's stock gang leader

explanation.surface: Someone sounds off about a mob boss who ends up gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' is not gunfire: shot silk changes colour as it moves, which is what opaline describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline means iridescent like an opal, the shimmering colour play of shot fabric.

clue.text: Fresh greens I'd eat at first, given vitality

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of eat
fresh signals the letters are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: Eating fresh vegetables first thing puts pep into you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' gives E from 'eat'; 'Fresh' rearranges GREENS and I'D to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Energised means filled with energy, invigorated or pepped up.

clue.text: Fabulous writer thus breaking a record

indicators.note: the word for thus breaks into the letters for a record, splitting them

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: An incredible author smashes a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means writing fables, not merely marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famed for fables about animals with morals attached.

clue.text: Former lord crushed by one's first spell in jail

indicators.note: the lord is squeezed between the other pieces, crushed inside them
first takes the opening letter of one

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence

explanation.surface: An ex-peer is squashed during his first stretch behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-time means belonging to an earlier era, of the past.

clue.text: One who regrets hiding key for person delivering

indicators.note: the regretful one hides the key within, holding it inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret, so a ruer regrets
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A remorseful person conceals a key belonging to a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivering' means saving from danger, not making deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from peril is to save them; a saviour does exactly that.

clue.text: Primate reportedly observed a Scotsman of great importance

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is as heard, matched by sound

parts.words: observed a Scotsman of great importance

explanation.surface: Someone apparently saw a very important Scot and called him an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mon' is the Scots pronunciation of man; 'spied a' said in a non-rhotic accent matches the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-limbed South American monkey with a prehensile tail is a primate.

clue.text: Cut down staff, getting sack

to axe is to sack, dismiss from a job

explanation.surface: Workers are cut and given the boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' reads as employees but means a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To poleaxe is to fell with a blow, as if struck by a battleaxe.

clue.text: They enjoy inflicting pain, like retired detectives way back

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

clue.text: Exceptionally, change Ernie's software

clue.text: Bloomer made by union leader in stiffly formal city

clue.text: Extremely ironic, my terms badly affecting both sides

extremely takes the extreme letters, first and last, of ironic

explanation.surface: Someone complains, very wryly, that their poor contract hurts both parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetric means balanced, the same on each half.

clue.text: Single-minded obsession of woman nursing Arab

an Omani, from Oman, is an Arab

clue.text: Accomplished youth takes directions, having too much to carry

clue.text: French composer right to abandon burlesque

clue.text: Spray shrub briefly with last of insecticide

clue.text: Mostly benevolent sergeant-major, a new member of the clan

clue.text: Loutishness of baddy finally replacing initiator of heist

explanation.definitionFit: A nine-sided polygon is a geometric shape, a plane figure.

clue.text: Calm air disorientated true provider of courses
